free_tier.stated: 'Start with $100 in free credits, no card required', with the page data carrying 'signupCredits: 100' and a footnote 'No card required'. The headline 'from $0.121/hr' is two discounts stacked: the tooltip says 'Melia 1 Pre-recorded base rate: $0.24, model training: -33%, top-tier annual commitment: -25%'. At the base Melia-1 pre-recorded rate of USD 0.24 an hour, 100 / 0.24 = 416 hours of batch transcription; at the Melia-1 real-time base of USD 0.40 an hour, 250 hours.

record.interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
record.chaining: a free CI runner plus USD 100 of batch transcription covers 416 hours of audio at the base rate, which is a podcast or lecture archive transcribed once. What breaks: the discount is paid for with training data or an annual commitment, and the enhanced-accuracy model at USD 0.75 an hour cuts the same credit to 133 hours.

limits.value: the credit is large and the discount ladder is the trap: the advertised USD 0.121 an hour requires opting into model training and a top-tier annual commitment, so a free account pays the USD 0.24 base rate and gets 416 hours rather than 826.

free_tier.stated: USD 100 credit grant at signup on the Free plan, no card required; one credit is worth one US dollar, and one balance covers Speech to Text, add-ons and Text to Speech. One-time, not a monthly allowance. Melia 1 pre-recorded base rate is USD 0.24 per hour.
free_tier.notes: models on the pricing page: Melia 1 (multilingual, 56 languages), Enhanced, Standard, Oak 1 (clinical language) and Linden 1 (voice agents), in batch (REST) and real-time (WebSocket) modes. unverified: whether the grant expires, because no vendor page read states a validity period; unverified: the rate for Text to Speech, which the pricing page names without a number

record.interface_detail: Batch REST API and real-time WebSocket API; an API key is created in the web portal; Python and JavaScript batch libraries
record.tooling: Python and JavaScript libraries, or raw HTTP and WebSocket with an API key created in the portal
record.chaining: the credit pays for batch transcription of recorded audio, which a free CI runner can post file by file; pair it with a free object store for the audio. The discounted headline rate on the pricing page needs a Pro plan with model training and a top-tier annual commitment, so a Free account pays the base rate.

limits.value: USD 100 credit grant at signup, one-time; Melia 1 pre-recorded base rate USD 0.24 per hour

Free plan real-time sessions are capped at 2 concurrent (Pro 50); the batch API asks for no more than 10 new jobs per second and 50 job-status requests per second, with a backstop of 20,000 concurrent jobs

record.binding_note: the one-time USD 100 credit is the ceiling for batch work; the 2 concurrent real-time sessions cap is a second wall for live audio

identity_cost.detail: no payment card on the Free plan ('no payment card required'); signup is an email with a password or a Google or GitHub account, and an email signup must verify the address by a link; unverified: whether a phone number is asked

record.reliability_note: the Free plan runs on the granted credit only; adding a payment card moves the account to Pro, where usage beyond the granted credits is charged to the card
record.confidence_note: the credit, the card-free Free plan, the signup methods and the real-time and batch limits are quoted from vendor pages; the credit's expiry and the text-to-speech rate are unverified.
